llm.summary: The skill's behavior largely matches a local semantic-memory plugin, but it asks to install npm binaries, write API keys to disk, read/migrate local memory files, and register recurring maintenance tasks — actions that are plausible for a memory service but have privacy/persistence implications that deserve caution.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (a replacement semantic memory system) aligns with its instructions: it installs an OpenClaw plugin, runs a local vector DB/service (Qdrant + cortex-mem-service), and requires LLM/embedding API keys. Minor inconsistency: setup claims only macOS Apple Silicon and Windows x64 supported but references Linux user data paths elsewhere.

dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions tell the agent to prompt the user for LLM and embedding API keys and to write them to config files in user data directories, to migrate existing OpenClaw memory (reads ~/.openclaw/workspace/memory), and to not proceed until local services are accessible. These operations involve reading and storing sensitive user data and local files — appropriate for migration but high-sensitivity and should be explicitly consented to.

dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill is instruction-only (no install spec), but it directs installing @memclaw/plugin and platform-specific @memclaw/bin-* packages from the npm registry. This is a moderate-risk install vector (npm packages and platform binaries), but there are no direct download URLs or obscure hosts in the instructions.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: It reasonably requires LLM and embedding API keys (expected), but those keys are stored in config.toml under user directories and are said to 'silently fall back to environment variables' if missing — yet the skill declares no required env vars. Storing keys on disk and silent fallback to env vars increases risk of accidental exposure; the skill does not declare or justify any unrelated credentials.

dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The plugin will auto-register a cron job running every 3 hours for maintenance, auto-start local services, and recommends disabling OpenClaw's built-in memory search. These introduce persistent behavior and scheduled background activity after installation (though always:true is not set). This persistence is plausible for a memory system but is a notable privilege and change to agent/system behavior.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be a real local memory plugin, but it will: (1) ask you to provide LLM and embedding API keys and write them to a config file under your user directory (plaintext risk), (2) install npm packages and platform binaries, (3) read and migrate existing OpenClaw memory files (may include sensitive content), and (4) register recurring maintenance (cron) tasks and auto-start services. Before installing, verify the plugin source (npm owner/package), consider installing in an isolated environment or VM, back up any existing memory, confirm you are comfortable storing API keys on disk (or prefer env vars), and review the actual plugin package code (or ask for the plugin's repository) to ensure there are no unexpected network endpoints or telemetry. If you need higher assurance, request the plugin's code or a signed release from a trusted homepage/source before proceeding.
